rows.question: My Limited Edition Beta copy of Lightning Bolt reads "Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Under current Oracle text, Lightning Bolt reads "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target." — it no longer says "one target."

Missing: The corpus contains no Comprehensive Rules paragraph defining "any target" and no rulings for this card (its `rulings` array is empty), so the exact scope of "any target" rests on the matching decision document, which is an unconfirmed model-assisted draft rather than a human-reviewed one.

Why: Your Beta card is the Limited Edition Beta printing, released 1993-10-04, whose original text is "Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target." The card's current Oracle text is "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target." The corpus flags this printing as a functional difference (reviewState "functional", similarity 0.600), and the matching decision says the change from "one target" to "any target" added planeswalkers and battles as legal targets. Note that all 20 printedVsOracle decisions in this corpus, including both Lightning Bolt entries, are marked model-assisted with confirmedByHuman false.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text under CR 108.1, which directs that the Oracle card reference determines a card's wording.

Quote [Oracle text]: Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target.

Quote [Limited Edition Beta printed text]: Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.

Quote [CR 108.1, CR 2026-09-25]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.

Quote [decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6 resolution]: Oracle governs under CR 108.1. "One target" became "any target", adding planeswalkers and battles. Similarity is 0.600, the high end of the set, yet the function changed.

Rules: 108.1

Conflict: The Beta printed text ("one target") disagrees with the current Oracle text ("any target"); Oracle wins under CR 108.1. The corpus holds no rule paragraph defining "any target," so that definitional detail is not independently corroborated here.

rows.question: My Limited Edition Alpha copy of False Orders reads "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Under current Oracle wording, False Orders removes a target creature the defending player controls from combat, unblocks anything that had become blocked solely by it, and then may have it block an attacking creature of your choice — it no longer lets you decide the defender's blocking.

Missing: None

Why: The Alpha card told the caster to decide whether and how one defending creature blocks. The current Oracle text does not dictate blocks at all; it takes a creature out of combat and lets you optionally re-assign it as a blocker, with a consequential unblocking clause. Oracle wording is what governs the card's function, so the printed and current texts are functionally different mechanics, not just rewording. A reviewed decision document exists for exactly this card and says the same thing, though it is a model-assisted draft not confirmed by a human, and its claims array is empty — the definite answer rests on the retrieved Oracle text itself.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), with CR 101.1 supplying card-over-general-rule precedence.

Quote [current Oracle text (card False Orders, currentAsOf 2026-09-18)]: "Cast this spell only during the declare blockers step.\nRemove target creature defending player controls from combat. Creatures it was blocking that had become blocked by only that creature this combat become unblocked. You may have it block an attacking creature of your choice."

Quote [printed text, Limited Edition Alpha (LEA) #147]: "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt."

Quote [ruling, published 2004-10-04]: "If a creature is removed from being a blocker of a given attacker, any triggered abilities that would have happened because it was declared as a blocker still happen."

Quote [rule 108.1]: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."

Quote [rule 101.1]: "Whenever a card's text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a)."

Quote [decision.False-Orders.0.083, resolution]: "Oracle governs under CR 108.1. Different mechanic. Printed dictates a defender's blocks; Oracle removes a creature from combat and may have it block, unblocking what it was blocking."

Rules: 108.1, 101.1

Conflict: The printed Alpha text (you decide the defender's blocks) contradicts the current Oracle text (remove a creature from combat, then optionally have it block). Under CR 108.1 the Oracle wording is the card's wording, and under CR 101.1 card text beats the general rules for the situation it covers; the Oracle text wins. No Comprehensive Rules paragraph on the declare blockers step, removing creatures from combat, or blocking was retrieved, so no rule number is cited for those mechanics.

Sources: card.38c5c952-8153-4d98-89b5-a75260383345, printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284, diff.printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284, decision.False-Orders.0.083, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, rule.101.1.2026-09-25, source.scryfall.2026-09-18

rows.question: My Unlimited Edition copy of Word of Command reads "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: The current Oracle text governs: Word of Command now gives you control of the target opponent until it finishes resolving (and through the resolution of any spell cast from the chosen card), and the printed "may not be countered" clause no longer exists.

Missing: None

Why: Under CR 108.1 the Oracle wording, not the printed wording, is the card's wording, so your Unlimited Edition text is overruled. The mechanism changed from "you make all the decisions it calls for" to actually controlling the player for the duration, and the Oracle text adds restrictions on which mana abilities can be activated that appear nowhere on the printed card. The old uncounterable clause is simply gone, so the spell can now be countered normally.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1.

Quote [Oracle — Word of Command, complete]: Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving.

Quote [Printed — Unlimited Edition (2ED), complete]: You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.

Quote [CR 108.1, complete]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.

Rules: 108.1

Conflict: The printed Unlimited Edition text says you make all the decisions and that the spell can't be countered after you look at the opponent's hand; the current Oracle text instead has you control the player (including through the resolution of a spell cast from the chosen card) and contains no uncounterable clause. CR 108.1 resolves this — Oracle wins.

Sources: card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443, diff.printing.239c8547-207b-41d1-a2be-8825bfc6ef7f, rule.108.1.2026-08-07, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, decision.Word-of-Command.0.257, case.pvo-2ED-Word-of-Command

rows.question: My Fourth Edition copy of Mana Vault reads "Mana Vault does not untap during your untap phase. If it remains tapped during your upkeep, Mana Vault deals 1 damage to you. {4}: Untap Mana Vault. Use this ability only during your upkeep. ocT: Add three colorless mana to your mana pool. Play these additions as interrupts.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Your Fourth Edition wording is superseded; under CR 108.1 the card's current Oracle text governs, so it doesn't untap in your untap step, you may pay {4} at the beginning of your upkeep to untap it (a triggered ability), it deals 1 damage to you at the beginning of your draw step if it's tapped, and it taps for {C}{C}{C}.

Missing: None

Why: Fourth Edition ("untap phase," an activated {4} untap usable during upkeep, and upkeep damage) no longer reflects how the card is played. The current Oracle text moves the damage to your draw step and turns the optional {4} untap into a triggered ability at the beginning of your upkeep. A reviewed adjudication document for this exact question confirms the Oracle text governs and must be reproduced in full.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording").

{4}: Untap Mana Vault. Use this ability only during your upkeep.
ocT: Add three colorless mana to your mana pool. Play these additions as interrupts."

At the beginning of your upkeep, you may pay {4}. If you do, untap this artifact.
At the beginning of your draw step, if this artifact is tapped, it deals 1 damage to you.
{T}: Add {C}{C}{C}."

Quote [CR 108.1]: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."

Quote [CR 101.1]: "Whenever a card's text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a)."

Rules: 108.1, 101.1

Conflict: The Fourth Edition printed text (upkeep damage, activated {4} untap during upkeep, "interrupt" timing) contradicts the current Oracle text (draw-step damage, triggered optional {4} untap at upkeep). The Oracle text wins under CR 108.1, so the printed wording does not describe the card's current function.

rows.question: Can Mogg Fanatic assign combat damage, sacrifice itself in response, and still deal that combat damage?
rows.answer:
Question type: interaction
Verdict: No. Under the current rules combat damage is assigned and then dealt as turn-based actions that don't use the stack, so there is no moment after Mogg Fanatic assigns damage but before it is dealt in which you could sacrifice it and still have that damage dealt.

Missing: None.

Why: Mogg Fanatic's sacrifice ability is an activated ability, and activating it requires priority. Rule 510.1 makes the announcement of combat damage assignment a turn-based action that doesn't use the stack, and rule 510.2 makes the dealing of that assigned damage a second turn-based action that also doesn't use the stack, with no player receiving the chance to cast spells or activate abilities in between. Because combat damage is no longer an object that goes on the stack, sacrificing Mogg Fanatic after it has assigned damage does not preserve the damage — this is exactly the case the reviewed decision document records as working before the Magic 2010 rules change in July 2009 and not working since. Note that the corpus's only rule paragraphs for 510 are the CR 2026-08-07 and CR 2026-09-25 versions, so the pre-July-2009 text of the combat damage step is not itself in the corpus; that half of the answer rests on the reviewed decision document.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text of Mogg Fanatic read with the current Comprehensive Rules — specifically CR 510.1 and CR 510.2, which govern the combat damage step — applied through the reviewed decision document case.rv-Mogg-Fanatic.

Quote [CR 510.1 — complete]: "First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. A player assigns a creature's combat damage according to the following rules:"

Quote [CR 510.2 — complete]: "Second, all combat damage that's been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time combat damage is assigned and the time it's dealt."

rows.question: When Word of Command resolves, who controls the opponent, and for how long?

Quote [Oracle text — Chaos Orb]: "{1}, {T}: If this artifact is on the battlefield, flip it onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot. If this artifact turns over completely at least once during the flip, destroy all nontoken permanents it touches. Then destroy this artifact."
Quote [verified adjudication case, expectedVerdict]: "Yes. Current Oracle text still requires flipping the card onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot, and it must turn over completely at least once. The wording was retemplated but the physical requirement remains."
Quote [CR 108.1]: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."
Quote [printed text — Limited Edition Alpha, for comparison]: "{1}: Flip Chaos Orb onto the playing area from a height of at least one foot. Chaos Orb must turn completely over at least once or it is discarded with no effect. When Chaos Orb lands, any cards in play that it touches are destroyed, as is Chaos Orb."
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: The printed wording and the current Oracle wording differ in cost and effect scope (Oracle adds {T} and excludes tokens), but neither removes the physical flip; Oracle wins under CR 108.1.

rows.question: The printed card just says 'Bands'. What does the card actually do, and did its function change?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: The Alpha printing's "Bands" is the banding ability in shorthand — the card's function has not changed; current Oracle text governs under CR 108.1 and spells the ability out in full.
Missing: None
Why: Your Alpha copy is Benalish Hero, whose printed text box reads only "Bands"; a reviewed decision document for this exact question states this is shorthand for banding and the function did not change, and the paired adjudication case instructs that the answer reproduce the current Oracle text and name the printing it overrules. The only oddity is measurement, not rules: the detected text similarity for the Alpha printing is 0.025 and its review state is "nonfunctional" — the low number reflects that a one-word shorthand does not look like a full reminder text, not a change in what the card does. Later printings (Fourth and Fifth Edition) kept the same ability but printed the keyword as "Banding"; note that the corpus contains a glossary entry cross-referencing rule 702.22, but that rule paragraph's text was not retrieved, so the banding rule itself is not quoted here.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text for Benalish Hero, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), with the reviewed decision case.rv-Benalish-Hero confirming the printed Alpha shorthand.
Quote [Oracle text — Benalish Hero, current as of 2026-09-18]: Banding (Any creatures with banding, and up to one without, can attack in a band. Bands are blocked as a group. If any creatures with banding you control are blocking or being blocked by a creature, you divide that creature's combat damage, not its controller, among any of the creatures it's being blocked by or is blocking.)
Quote [Printed text — Limited Edition Alpha, 1993-08-05]: Bands
Quote [Printed text — Limited Edition Beta, 1993-10-04]: Bands
Quote [Printed text — Unlimited Edition, 1993-12-01]: Bands

Quote [Printed text — Fifth Edition, 1997-03-24]: Banding
Quote [CR 108.1, CR 2026-09-25]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card’s wording. A card’s Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Quote [Glossary — Banding, "Bands with Other"]: Banding is a keyword ability that modifies the rules for declaring attackers and assigning combat damage. “Bands with other” is a specialized version of the ability. See rule 702.22, “Banding.”
Quote [Ruling 2008-10-01]: If a creature with banding attacks, it can team up with any number of other attacking creatures with banding (and up to one nonbanding creature) and attack as a unit called a "band." If a creature with banding is blocked, the attacking player chooses how the blockers' damage is assigned.

rows.question: My Alpha Lightning Bolt says 'one target'. Can I still point it at a planeswalker?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Yes — under current Oracle wording your Lightning Bolt reads "any target," which includes planeswalkers, so the Alpha printed wording "one target" does not limit what you may target.

Missing: None for the verdict. One gap worth flagging: the paragraph text of CR 115.4 is not present in the retrieved corpus — only its number, appearing as a cross-reference inside the glossary definition of "Any Target." The substance is supplied by that glossary definition and by CR 108.1.

Why: Rule 108.1 says to use the Oracle card reference to determine a card's wording, so the physical Alpha printing's text is not what governs play. The Oracle text for Lightning Bolt is "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target," and "any target" is defined as "target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle." That makes the Alpha "one target" phrasing merely a change in wording and scope, not a restriction you must keep playing under.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text for Lightning Bolt, read under CR 108.1 (Oracle governs wording); the scope of "any target" is fixed by the Comprehensive Rules glossary term "Any Target." This is backed by two verified adjudication cases, case.pvo-LEB-Lightning-Bolt (printedVsOracle) and case.rv-Lightning-Bolt (rulesVersion).

Quote Oracle text (Lightning Bolt): "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target."

Quote Printed text (Limited Edition Alpha, collector no. 161, released 1993-08-05): "Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target."

Quote Glossary term "Any Target": "A spell or ability may require "any target." "Any target" is the same as "target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle." See rule 115.4."

Quote CR 108.1: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."

Quote CR 101.1: "Whenever a card's text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a)."

Quote Verified case case.pvo-LEB-Lightning-Bolt (expectedVeridct): "Current Oracle text governs under CR 108.1: "Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target." The answer must reproduce this text completely and name the printing it overrules."

Quote Verified case case.rv-Lightning-Bolt (expectedVerdict): "Yes. Current Oracle text reads 'any target', which includes planeswalkers and battles. Measured text similarity to the printed wording is 0.600, high, yet the function changed. Oracle governs under CR 108.1."

Rules: 108.1, 101.1 (both retrieved as full paragraph text); 115.4 (number retrieved only, as a cross-reference inside the glossary definition of "Any Target" — the paragraph itself is not in the corpus and I am not quoting it)

Conflict: The Alpha printing ("one target") disagrees textually with current Oracle ("any target"), and CR 108.1 resolves it in favour of Oracle. Separately, decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6 reaches the same conclusion but is a model-assisted, human-unconfirmed draft, while case.pvo-LEB-Lightning-Bolt and case.rv-Lightning-Bolt are marked verified; the verified cases control, and they agree with the draft.
